name: Bayland Marina
summary: Slip rentals, transient dockage and a fuel dock on the Houston Ship Channel at Baytown, just inside a marked channel past marker 100.

hero.eyebrow: Slip rentals and transient dockage in Baytown
hero.title: Your cruising destination
hero.lead: Bayland Marina is back in service. Renovations to the docks and the marina are finished, and we are now accepting lease applications for slips from 35 to 55 feet.

groups.title: Slip Rentals
groups.summary: Slips from 35 to 55 feet, month to month or on a three-month lease.
groups.intro: Slips run from 35 to 55 feet, and we are now accepting lease applications. Please call for availability, and larger vessels should make advanced reservations. Water is furnished and electricity is metered at commercial rates.
groups.imageAlt: New floating docks with power pedestals, looking back toward the marina buildings

services.title: Month to Month Slips
services.text: Monthly rates run from $260 for a 35-foot slip to $390 for a 55-foot slip, effective May 2020.

services.title: Three Month and Longer Leases
services.text: A three-month or longer lease takes $10 off the monthly rate at every slip length.
points: We are now accepting lease applications

services.title: Deposit and Insurance
services.text: A deposit of one month's rent plus $35.00 is due with the lease, and $300,000 liability insurance is required to rent a slip.
points: Electricity metered at commercial rates, water furnished

services.title: Larger Vessels
services.text: Vessels larger than 55 feet must make advanced reservations. Call the marina manager to talk through what is open.

groups.title: Transient Dockage
groups.summary: Transients welcome at $2.00 per boat foot per night.
groups.intro: We welcome transients. The nightly rate is $2.00 per boat foot, and the marina sits about 12 miles from the Kemah Boardwalk, just inside a marked channel off the Houston Ship Channel. Call ahead and the harbor master will tell you where to tie up.

services.title: Nightly Dockage
services.text: Transient boats are charged $2.00 per boat foot per day, with the same water and metered power as a leased slip.

services.title: Coming In By Water
services.text: Enter the Houston Ship Channel before HSC marker 89 and follow on toward marker 100. The entrance to the marina is a marked channel just past marker 100, through a high range and a low range marker.
points: Past the Bayport channel it is open water toward Morgans Point
The water can be skinny at low tides
There is a shallow spot at the marina entrance, so swing wide before heading into the docks

services.title: Advance Reservations
services.text: Larger vessels must make advanced reservations. Call ahead and we will confirm what is open before you make the run.

groups.title: Fuel Dock and Marina Store

groups.intro: The fuel dock is open during regular business hours, and the marina store has been renovated along with the rest of the marina. The office is on site, so there is someone to talk to when you come in.
groups.imageAlt: The marina store and office buildings seen across the water from the docks

services.title: Fuel Dock

services.title: Marina Store

services.title: Marina Office

points: Open 8 AM to 5 PM, Tuesday through Sunday

groups.intro: Bayland Marina has been restored beyond her former glory: new docks, storm surge security platforms and a renovated marina store. The harbormaster keeps the rules that make the marina safe for everyone tied up here.

promo.title: Tie up for the night on your way through the ship channel.
promo.text: Transient boats are welcome at the nightly rate, about 12 miles from the Kemah Boardwalk and just past HSC marker 100.

about.title: Bayland Marina is back in service.
text: Hello fellow boaters. Bayland Marina is back in service. Renovations to the docks and the marina are now finished, and Bayland Marina has been restored beyond her former glory: new docks, storm surge security platforms and a renovated marina store.

We are now accepting lease applications for slips from 35 to 55 feet, and we welcome transients at $2.00 per boat foot per night. If you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact the marina manager.
Bob Hartquist is the harbor master, and Tim and Tom Hazelwood own the marina. Please feel free to navigate our website and forward this site to fellow boaters.
about.imageAlt: The marina office building at the head of the walkway down to the docks

values.title: New docks
values.text: The docks and the marina have been renovated and are back in service.

values.title: Storm surge platforms
values.text: Storm surge security platforms were built in as part of the renovation.

values.title: A safe marina
values.text: Rules and regulations are kept so everyone has a safe and enjoyable time at the marina.

faqs.a: Rates effective May 2020: 35′ $260, 40′ $300, 45′ $335, 50′ $360 and 55′ $390 a month, and $10 a month less on each at a three-month or longer lease. Please call for availability.
Yes. We welcome transients at $2.00 per boat foot per night. Larger vessels must make advanced reservations.

faqs.q: What is needed to rent a slip?
faqs.a: A deposit of one month's rent plus $35.00, and $300,000 liability insurance. Water is furnished and electricity is metered at commercial rates.

faqs.q: Is there fuel at the marina?
faqs.a: Yes. The fuel dock is open during regular business hours.

faqs.q: How do I find the entrance from the water?
faqs.a: Enter the Houston Ship Channel before HSC marker 89 and follow toward marker 100. The entrance is a marked channel just past marker 100, through a high range and a low range marker. The water can be skinny at low tides and there is a shallow spot at the entrance, so swing wide before you head into the docks.

facts.heading: Driving here
items: From Houston near I-45: I-45 South to I-610 East toward TX-225/Pasadena, exit TX-225 East/La Porte, go left at the fork and follow signs for TX-146 North/Baytown, over the Fred Hartman Bridge, then take the first exit for TX-146 Business North

From Houston near I-10: I-10 East to TX-330 Spur South/Baytown, then TX-146 South, exit Missouri St/Waterfront District, merge onto Robert C. Lanier Dr (feeder road) and continue onto TX-146 Business North
From Kemah, La Porte and Clear Lake: TX-146 North over the Fred Hartman Bridge, first exit for TX-146 Business North

From Beaumont: I-10 West to TX-99 Grand Parkway South (tolls may apply), TX-99 South to TX-146 Business, left at the stop sign onto TX-146 Business South, left at the Missouri signal light into the marina entrance
At the first signal light the marina entrance is on your right — turn in and follow down toward the docks

facts.heading: Rules and regulations
items: So that everyone has a safe and enjoyable time at Bayland Marina, boaters and their companions are asked to adhere to the marina's rules and regulations
To ensure safety, certain rules and regulations must be observed and enforced; violations may be cause for eviction and/or other appropriate legal action

Anyone causing damage to or destroying public property of any kind, including buildings, fixtures or appurtenances, whether through violation of the rules or through any act or omission, is fully liable to the City, and the damage must be reported immediately to the harbormaster

Anyone involved in an accident at the marina or in the vicinity resulting in personal injury or damage to vessels, docks or aids to navigation must report it to the harbormaster, or a designated representative, within ten days
An accident report must include, but is not limited to, the names and addresses of all principals and witnesses, if known, and a statement of the facts

Commercial vessels operating from the municipal marina that are involved in any accident resulting in personal injury or damage to other vessels, docks or aids to navigation must report it immediately to the harbormaster

Unless a lease or other contractual agreement provides otherwise, no area of the marina, including buildings whether privately or publicly owned, may be used to store cargo or any other property or equipment without the harbormaster's permission
If an area is used for storage without that permission, the harbormaster may order the cargo or property removed, or have it removed and stored at the expense of the owner or consignee

The rules and regulations for craft owners and lessees are set out in sections covering definitions, compliance with the rules, insurance certificates, responsibility for damages, non-vessel storage of equipment and hours of operation
The insurance certificates section is pending changes
